title: myrobalanus oblonga
intro: Myrobalanus oblonga, commonly known as Terminalia chebula, is a deciduous tree native to the Indian subcontinent, belonging to the Combretaceae family. It has been traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to provide various health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can help alleviate digestive issues, boost the immune system, and protect against oxidative stress. The bioactive constituents of Terminalia chebula include chebulagic acid, corosolic acid, and flavonoids, which exhibit therapeutic actions such as inhibiting the growth of pathogens, protecting against cardiovascular diseases, and promoting wound healing. Additionally, Terminalia chebula is used to reduce oxidative stress, protect against cancer, and exhibit neuroprotective effects.
